case_scope: United States auto finance, negative equity, repossession, and mobility asset fragility

household_market_extraction_gate.note: Auto debt is large and current delinquency/repo/negative-equity evidence makes vehicle access a fragile wealth rail unless loss mitigation, add-on controls, and deficiency protections work.

auto_finance_negative_equity.note: Negative-equity rollover can make the replacement vehicle underwater from day one and increase deficiency-balance risk after default or repossession. Rev0344 unused-source burn-down: Federal Reserve G.19 consumer-credit data is now bound to auto/consumer-credit exposure.

auto_repossession_mobility_loss.note: Repossession is a threshold harm because it can remove the work/care transportation rail while leaving fees, deficiency balances, and credit damage behind.

transportation_access_cost_burden.note: Car dependence intensifies auto-finance risk when transit substitutes are weak.

consumer_credit_fee_drag.note: Auto delinquency must be scored with broader consumer-delinquency dynamics and credit-card/student-loan/mortgage spillovers.

household_market_remedy_access.note: The case lacks hard evidence that cure notices, loss mitigation, auction surplus, add-on refunds, and deficiency-balance defenses arrive before work access is lost.

proof_debt: repossession by subgroup, credit tier, geography, and lender type
deficiency balances, fees, and collection after auction
negative-equity rollover rates and loan-to-value by replacement vehicle
force-placed insurance, GAP, service-contract, and add-on refund outcomes
work/care mobility loss after repossession and availability of transit substitutes

gate_16_household_market_extraction.why: Necessary transportation cannot be counted as secure household wealth while repossession, negative equity, and deficiency debt can remove the job/care rail.

gate_15_place_public_finance.why: Auto-finance risk worsens where transit substitutes are weak and car loss immediately threatens work and care access.

evidence_debt_register.question: repossession by subgroup, credit tier, geography, and lender type
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Use CFPB auto-finance pilot data and household-credit releases to identify where repossession concentrates and how quickly it follows delinquency.

evidence_debt_register.question: deficiency balances and post-auction collection
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Measure remaining balances, fees, collection suits, credit reporting, and wage/bank collection after vehicle sale.

evidence_debt_register.question: negative-equity rollover rates
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Track loan-to-value, trade-in shortfall, term length, and recurrence of underwater replacement loans.

evidence_debt_register.question: add-on and force-placed insurance incidence
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Collect dealer/lender data on service contracts, GAP, credit insurance, force-placed products, refunds, and cancellation friction.

evidence_debt_register.question: mobility substitution after repossession
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Match repo geography with job density, transit availability, child/elder care access, and ride-cost burden.

policy_pathway: Score auto finance as mobility collateral, not just consumer credit.
Require pre-repossession cure/loss-mitigation evidence, negative-equity controls, add-on refund enforcement, transparent auctions, and deficiency-balance limits before lowering Gate 16.
